title: Register your business name with DTI
timing: Before applying for the barangay clearance and business permit.
steps: Go to the BNRS website and click New Registration.
Provide the required information and review it.
Submit the application.
Pay the registration fee for your territorial scope (Barangay ₱200, City/Municipality ₱500, Regional ₱1,000, National ₱2,000) plus ₱30 documentary stamp tax.
documents: One valid government-issued ID of the applicant
Tax Identification Number (TIN) of the owner, if applicable
Duly accomplished DTI Business Name Registration Application Form
Authorization letter and valid ID of the representative, if filed through a representative
Non-Philippine nationals, if applicable: certified copy of Alien Certificate of Registration (ACR) and Certificate of Authority to engage in business in the Philippines

title: Get barangay business clearance
timing: Before applying for the local business permit; details vary by barangay.
steps: Apply at the barangay where the business is located.
Submit the business registration document, if applicable, proof of right to occupy the premises and a government ID.
Pay the local fee and keep the official receipt.
documents: Valid ID (National ID, Passport, Driver's License, or Voter's ID)
Proof of residency
Community Tax Certificate (cedula)
Application form (provided at the barangay hall)

title: Apply for a business permit
timing: Before operations; fees and requirements depend on the city or municipality.
steps: Prepare business registration and the basis for computing local fees.
Prepare occupancy permit if required, lease contract if renting, and barangay clearance as applicable.
File with the concerned local government unit.
documents: Application form from the local Business Permits and Licensing Department
DTI certificate
Barangay clearance
Notarized contract of lease, if renting
Transfer Certificate of Title (TCT) or Tax Declaration, if the property is owned
Community Tax Certificate (cedula)
Photos of the establishment (front, right and left sides, including the road)
Locational/zoning clearance
Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (BFP)
Sanitary permit (local health office)
Certificate of occupancy
Public liability insurance, for high-traffic places

title: Register with BIR
timing: At the registration stage; confirm filing method and requirements with the assigned RDO.
steps: Use the available online registration route or file BIR Form 1901 at the assigned RDO.
For manual filing, prepare a government ID and the required invoice option.
Check the certificate of registration and the tax types assigned to the business.
documents: Any government-issued ID (e.g. PhilID/ePhilID, Passport, Driver's License)
Additional proof of residence or business address, if the ID has no address
Final clear sample of your own invoices, or a BIR-printed invoice (BPI)
DTI certificate, if you have a registered business name

title: Register the employer and employees
timing: When hiring staff; registration itself is generally one-time.
steps: Get an SSS employer number through the available portal or SSS branch.
For manual filing prepare Form R-1 and business identification.
Report employees and ensure they have SS numbers.
documents: SSS Employer Registration Form (R-1), if applicable
Employment Report (R-1A)
DTI Certificate of Business Name Registration
Valid government-issued ID of the business owner/employer
Tax Identification Number (TIN) of the employer
Business/Mayor's Permit, if applicable
Certification and Agreement on Data Privacy Notice
Letter of Authority (LOA) or Special Power of Attorney (SPA), if filed through an authorized representative
For employees: SS number, or SSS Personal Record (E-1/E-1V) if none yet
Valid ID/supporting documents of employees, when required

title: Register employer and employees
timing: When hiring staff; registration itself is generally one-time.
steps: Register the employer with PhilHealth.
Report newly hired employees and arrange premium remittance.
documents: PhilHealth Employer Data Record (ER1)
DTI Certificate of Business Name Registration
BIR Certificate of Registration (Form 2303), when required
Valid government-issued ID of the business owner/authorized signatory
Business/Mayor's Permit, when applicable
Authorization letter and valid IDs, if filed through a representative
For employees: PhilHealth Identification Number (PIN), or PhilHealth Member Registration Form (PMRF) if none yet
Report of Employee-Members (ER2)

title: Register as an employer
timing: When hiring staff; registration itself is generally one-time.
steps: Register the employer with Pag-IBIG Fund.
Prepare employee membership details for subsequent remittances.
documents: Employer's Data Form (EDF), HQP-PFF-002
DTI Certificate of Business Name Registration
Proof of business existence
Valid government-issued ID of the business owner/employer
Business/Mayor's Permit, when applicable
Authorization letter and valid IDs, if filed through a representative
For employees: Pag-IBIG Membership ID (MID) number, or Member's Data Form (MDF) for new members
Employee personal and employment information

title: Renew your DTI business name
timing: After 5 years from the validity date. Late renewal is charged an additional 50%.
steps: Go to the BNRS website.
Click Renewal and provide the required information.
Review the information provided.
Submit the renewal application.
Complete the required payment.
documents: Business name registration details for the BNRS renewal form

title: Renew barangay clearance
steps: Go to the designated office or Business One-Stop Shop (BOSS) of your city or municipality.
Submit the documents required for renewing the barangay business clearance, as specified by the LGU.
Pay the barangay clearance fee, if required.
Receive the renewed Barangay Business Clearance or proof of clearance.
documents: Existing clearance and locally required supporting papers

title: Renew the local business permit
timing: Valid for 1 year. Renew within the first month of the year or on the anniversary date of the permit's issuance.
steps: Prepare the basis for computing local taxes and fees, such as income tax returns.
Submit renewed barangay clearance and other local requirements.
Pay the assessment and retain the renewed permit.
documents: Basis for local taxes and fees
Barangay clearance
Existing business permit

title: File the applicable tax returns
timing: Income tax is commonly annual and quarterly; exact forms and schedules depend on taxpayer classification and registration.
steps: Confirm registered tax types on the BIR certificate of registration.
Determine the applicable income, VAT or percentage, and withholding tax returns.
File required returns and pay tax due by the applicable deadlines.
documents: Certificate of Registration
Applicable BIR tax return

title: Remit SSS and EC contributions
timing: Monthly; exact payment schedule depends on current SSS rules.
steps: Compute the employer and employee SSS shares and employer EC contribution.
Remit the amounts through an accepted channel and keep proof of payment.
documents: Payroll and contribution schedule

title: Remit PhilHealth premiums
timing: Monthly; confirm current remittance and reporting schedule.
steps: Compute employer and employee premium shares.
Remit premiums and submit required reports.
documents: Payroll and remittance records

title: Remit Pag-IBIG savings
timing: Monthly; confirm current remittance and reporting schedule.
steps: Compute employer and employee membership savings.
Remit savings and submit the Membership Savings Remittance Form as required.
documents: Payroll records
MSRF when required
